narrative.overview:
This scoped reference records the implemented [character studio](index.html), its [stylesheet](studio.css), and its [runtime](studio.js). It inherits the blue actions, native typography, clear labels, and flat utility surfaces of the root [design system](../../../DESIGN.md). It does not replace that system or choose MERLIN's final application platform.

The authored midnight scene supplies the visual character. MERLIN retains the original rounded proportions, matte/satin blue surfaces, flush dark display, pale cyan face details, and lit feet. The surrounding interface stays compact so the animated character and editable physical screens remain easy to inspect. Blender is the visual lighting reference; the browser's floor, lights, shadows, and bloom approximate it.
keyCharacteristics: Native controls and restrained blue actions on a pale neutral page.
A fixed landscape stage that preserves the authored camera composition.
Explicit animation status, playback controls, and editable screen content.
A large local time and small date that keep clear of the character and pulled panels.
Optional compact timer and music cards borrow the existing white panel family and yield to the clock and character.
A separate local preview with honest boundaries around unconnected services.

rules.name: The Clear Slot Rule
rules.body: Keep the current resting anchor whenever its measured text bounds remain clear across the planned motion. Replan on motion-route or size changes; do not chase each rendered pose. Precomputed [motion footprints](motion-footprints.json) reserve the full destination loop and the active route segment, including the walk back in the opposite direction, return transitions, and panel dismissal shards. When moving between opposite panels, retain clearance for the old panel through dismissal, then replan at the shared ready pose before the next pull. If all anchors overlap, choose the least-obstructed anchor with a small stability tolerance.

rules.name: The Optional Space Rule
rules.body: Reserve the clock before floating cards, preserve a safe anchor, and conceal a card with retained data whenever no clear anchor remains. Full-face entry, substates, and exit, ceiling presentations, and busy paired-screen transitions share the clock's concealment policy. Concealed cards are inert and removed from accessibility APIs; clearing them while concealed prevents restoration.

dos: **Do** preserve the original character proportions, matte materials, pale cyan display detail, and 4:3 composition.
**Do** retain labeled native controls, visible keyboard focus, textual status, and explicit playback control.
**Do** keep screen editing separate from animation selection and preserve content on the correct surface and fragments.
**Do** label the browser lighting as an approximation and use Blender as the visual reference.
**Do** retain a clear clock anchor across the complete planned motion, including reverse walking and panel dismissal, and hide the clock throughout full-face and ceiling entry, substates, and exit.
**Do** keep clock movement brief and use immediate placement when reduced motion is requested.
**Do** keep floating cards optional, reserve the clock first, and retain concealed card data until space returns or the caller removes it.
**Do** keep floating controls at (44 × 44px), expose clear state text, and wait for caller-confirmed updates.
donts: **Don't** treat camera, searching, or music gestures as proof of live camera, search, or music integration.
**Don't** turn a textured screen into a claim of clickable DOM, persisted content, or uploaded images.
**Don't** expand this local preview into a product-platform decision or claim tested production-device performance.
**Don't** replace the original authored asset with stock or generated substitute artwork. The six Blender state stills carry embedded provenance; owner reference screenshots are not redistributed.
**Don't** turn a floating sample into automatic timer execution, audible music, saved state, or live companion integration.
